competition.resource_limits_note: SubmissionSizeLimit/AgentDisk/AgentRam/AgentCpuCores are unresolved template placeholders in the live 'How to Submit' API page and are not present in the open-source kaggle_environments cabt.json env spec; could not be resolved to concrete numbers this phase. Archive built is 1.92MB, well within any typical Kaggle simulation-competition norm. Flagged as a known limitation.

layer_a_deck_selection.method: tools/build_agent_layer_a_deck_selection_v1.py, applying the frozen Phase 4.6 policy (results/meta/final_deck_selection_policy.csv) restricted to decks with both real ladder data and a tested hand-tuned Layer B policy
layer_a_deck_selection.selection_basis: Recent WR (14d real-ladder snapshot) among eligible candidates; tied on point estimate with Mega Lucario ex (61.67% n=60 vs 57.07% n=184, Wilson 95% CIs overlap), tie-broken toward Dragapult ex on sample-size/precision grounds
layer_a_deck_selection.counter_rule_reason: The only OOS_CONFIRMED validated counter (Team Rocket's Mewtwo ex -> Fezandipiti ex) does not involve Dragapult ex as the counter archetype; not activated.

layer_b_gameplay_policy.base_agent: src.agents.dragapult_agent (751-line hand-tuned port of the official notebook agent)

going_first_second_override.basis: Pre-existing dedicated controlled experiment (results/dragapult_first_second_analysis.md): 1000 games/condition, Dragapult ex significantly better going first vs Abomasnow ex (67.1% vs 56.3%, z=-4.97), never significantly worse vs any tested opponent. Corroborated (not solely established) by this phase's real-ladder pooled analysis (results/agent/going_first_second_analysis.csv): POOLED first-player advantage +8.62pp, Wilson 95% CI [6.29%, 10.96%], credible=True.
going_first_second_override.layer_a_usage: NOT used to adjust Layer A expected-win-rate deck ranking -- Dragapult ex's own archetype-level real-ladder advantage (+6.6pp, n=137/200) is not individually statistically credible (Wilson CI includes 0) at current sample size, per Section 7's 'do not use for deck selection if underpowered' rule. Retained purely as an in-game (Layer B) feature.

bayesian_opponent_prediction.basis: results/agent/opponent_prediction_notes.md, results/agent/opponent_prediction_metrics.csv. Beats the recent-meta-prior baseline decisively from turn 2 onward (top-1 77.0%/85.1%/87.2% at turns 2/3/full vs 35.0% baseline; log loss 1.237/0.852/0.665 vs 1.961), but turn-1 log loss is worse than baseline, only 43% of the canonical 3,499-episode dataset had turn-by-turn data available (1,503 episodes), 4/11 archetypes trained on <20 examples, and only one temporal train/test split was run.
bayesian_opponent_prediction.production_hook: None exists for Dragapult ex specifically -- dragapult_agent.py's hand-tuning operates at the individual-opposing-Pokemon level, not the archetype level, so there is no validated archetype-level tactical delta to condition on. Model is built/tested/documented but intentionally not called from main.py this cycle (Section 36: don't add complexity without a validated benefit).

validated_counter_integration.reason: No OOS_CONFIRMED counter exists with Dragapult ex as the counter archetype.

timeout_shield.match_budget_source: kaggle_environments cabt.json observation.remainingOverageTime=600, cross-confirmed against docs/environment.md's independently C++-engine-sourced '10 minutes per match total' finding

safety.exception_shield: Composed via safety_wrapper (catches exceptions from the wrapped inner agent, including any raised inside timeout_shield's thread) and timeout_shield (catches inner-agent exceptions separately from timeouts). Measured 0 exceptions across all ablation runs.

jaccard_experiment.reason: No decision this phase depended on refining archetype representation beyond the existing canonical SHA-256-based deck_to_archetype.csv mapping (reused as-is throughout); Section 26 makes this experiment explicitly conditional ('if useful'). Time budget prioritized toward engine-integration/safety work given the 2026-08-16 deadline.

glicko_experiment.reason: Section 27 explicitly instructs: 'if player identity/rating data is structurally unreliable, do not attempt to reconstruct player Glicko-2.' Phase 4.1/4.5b/4.6 already established, across three independent sessions, that per-side rating cannot be reliably resolved from this dataset (~49-53% labeled-check accuracy, indistinguishable from chance) -- a structural, not sample-size, limitation. An archetype-strength alternative would substantially duplicate Phase 4.3/4.3b's already-completed (and largely negative) strategy-comparison work.

rl_experiment.reason: Section 28 gate: simulator supports the interaction model (yes, Search API exists) and a working non-RL candidate already exists (yes), but insufficient time remains before the 2026-08-16 deadline to build and strictly-OOS-validate an RL/contextual-bandit candidate against the existing agent within this same phase. Not attempted.
